verdict.reasoning: REFUTED on four independent grounds. (1) NOTHING IS MISSING. The finding is filed as kind=missing-heading, but the heading is present verbatim. The 300dpi render of page 1146 prints the bold heading 'D.19.5.3 Conformance'; specs/ISO_COBOL.md:46090 reads '## D.19.5.3 Conformance', preceded at :46089 by the machine-readable anchor ''. Clause number and title are both intact, plus a normalized anchor id encoding the full dotted number. I also diffed the whole page body against the render: every element is present and verbatim — the D.19.5.3 opening paragraph ('Conformance allows the compiler to check the application code...'), 'EXAMPLE:', 'One part of a banking application...', the code line '01 an-account USAGE OBJECT REFERENCE Account.', 'can reference any object of the account class...', 'A different part of the banking application...', 'NOTE In this example, no classes inherit from the CheckingAccount class.', '01 an-account USAGE OBJECT REFERENCE CheckingAccount.', 'If a source element contains code...', 'The policy for conformance checking is conservative and errs on the side of caution.', and 'These are some examples of restrictions imposed by compile time conformance checking...'. Zero characters of page 1146 are absent from the transcription. (2) THE CLAIM MISQUOTES THE SIBLING SET. It states D.19.5.3 is at level 2 'while sibling D.19.5.1 is at level 3', framing D.19.5.3 as the lone outlier that was 'lifted out of D.19.5'. But D.19.5.2 is ALSO at markdown level 2: specs/ISO_COBOL.md:46074 reads '## D.19.5.2 Restricting inheritance and modification with the FINAL clause'. Of the three siblings, TWO are at level 2 and ONE is at level 3 — so if anything D.19.5.1 is the outlier, and the claim's own reasoning would invert. The stated sibling contrast is factually wrong as written. (3) THE CLAIMED HARM IS FALSE — markdown heading depth is not a clause-nesting signal anywhere in this transcription, so nothing is 'lost'. I tallied all 305 numbered Annex-D headings by (clause depth -> markdown level): depth-4 clauses appear at level 2 seventy-nine times, at level 3 forty-eight times, at level 4 only eight times; depth-3 clauses appear at level 2 sixty-one times vs level 3 twenty-four times; depth-5 at level 2 twenty-six times vs level 3 twenty-three times. 'D.19.5.3 at level 2' is an instance of the single MOST COMMON pattern in the annex (depth-4 -> level 2, 79 occurrences), not a break. The recurring shape is that the first subclause after a parent keeps a deeper level and later siblings collapse to level 2 — visible identically at D.2.2.1/D.2.2.2, D.3.5.2/D.3.5.3, D.19.3.2/D.19.3.3, D.19.4.1/D.19.4.2, and D.19.5.4.1/D.19.5.4.2. Furthermore, level 2 is simultaneously used for the page-break banners ('## Page 1146' at :46086) and level 1 for the running header ('# ISO/IEC 1989:2023 (E)' at :46087), so heading depth in this file is already unusable as a clause tree by construction. Any extractor must key on the heading TEXT or the '' anchor — both of which are correct here. The clause numbering is fully recoverable. (4) IT IS FORMATTING, NOT CONTENT. A markdown '#' count is presentation metadata added by the transcriber; it carries no ISO normative meaning, and Annex D is informative in any case. No word, number, symbol, rule, or relationship of the standard differs between the PDF page and the markdown. This falls squarely under the rejection criteria 'the difference is only ... formatting' and 'the difference does not change meaning'. A global heading-depth normalization pass over Annex D would be a reasonable cosmetic cleanup, but it is a transcription-style item affecting ~190 headings uniformly — not a page-1146 PDF-vs-markdown discrepancy, and not structural severity.
verdict.corrected_description: Not a discrepancy. The heading 'D.19.5.3 Conformance' is present in the markdown verbatim at specs/ISO_COBOL.md:46090 with its anchor '<a id="section-d-19-5-3">', and the entire page-1146 body matches the render word for word. The report's premise is also wrong: D.19.5.2 (:46074) is at markdown level 2 too, so D.19.5.3 is not an outlier among its siblings. Markdown heading depth does not encode clause depth anywhere in this transcription — across 305 numbered Annex-D headings, depth-4 clauses sit at level 2 (79x), level 3 (48x) and level 4 (8x), and level 2 is also used for page banners ('## Page 1146') — so no clause numbering is lost; it lives in the heading text and the anchor id. At most this is a cosmetic, file-wide heading-level normalization item, not a page-1146 content defect.
